register.level: mock-genteel host's manners used as a weapon; clipped and contrary
register.summary: The Hatter's echo and foil, speaking the shortest lines in the cast (median 4 words). He offers what isn't there ('Have some wine' / 'There isn't any'), lectures on etiquette he himself breaks, repeats himself when cornered ('It was the best butter'), and in court denies everything flatly.

examples.text: It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited,

catchphrases.text: Have some wine / Take some more tea

sentence_style.length: very short (mean 6.8 words, median 4); fragments, one-word dates, flat denials

patterns.rule: Hollow hospitality: offers of food and drink that are empty or absurd.
Etiquette rebukes and pedantic corrections of Alice's wording (civil, invited, say what you mean, you might just as well say).

examples.text: Then you should say what you mean,
You might just as well say, that 'I like what I get' is the same thing as 'I get what I like'!
Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?

patterns.rule: Stubborn repetition and flat contradiction, escalating to outright denial in court.

examples.text: It was the best butter, you know.

patterns.rule: Refers to Alice in the third person as 'the young lady' and pushes the group's whims ('I vote…', 'Suppose we change the subject').

examples.text: Suppose we change the subject, I'm getting tired of this. I vote the young lady tells us a story.

address.self: I; 'us' for the tea-party ('Tell us a story!')
address.to_alice: you, or 'the young lady' in the third person

examples.text: I vote the young lady tells us a story.

forbidden_words.reason: his manners are always a rebuke, never real; he never concedes a point (ends every exchange in 'Why not?' or a denial)

forbidden_words.regex: \b(for instance|once upon a time|suppose it were)\b
forbidden_words.reason: extended explanation belongs to the Hatter (Time and the clock) and storytelling to the Dormouse; the Hare stays clipped

drift.change: Tea-party: contrary host, hollow offers, etiquette rebukes.
Court witness: reduced to one-word dates and flat denials ('Fifteenth,', 'I didn't!', 'I deny it!').

backtest_markers.regex: \b(civil|invited|say what you mean|you might just as well say|do you mean)\b
^(I didn't|I deny it|why not|nor I|I only wish it was|fifteenth)\b
\b(tell us a story|change the subject|I vote|young lady)\b

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test: a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse (recited text) excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb1/result.json#backtest_method
